project.name: Law review subject tags
project.tagline: Every law review paper on our list gets its abstract or first pages; our own model then tags each paper with its subjects, and the tags go paper -> professor -> school on the law school rankings site.

headline.sentence: Phase 2 of 5 (Labels) is the focus now: Silver S1 coding at 15 of 317 units. Phase 1 (Collect) and Phase 3 (Model) keep running beside it. 3 of 3 jobs that must keep running are running. Next milestone: the v0.9 beta, estimated 2026-11-22 to 2026-12-02.

coverage.how: the CORE lane's target list: every paper without a usable text after the s18 plan with the side stores (weak texts counted as missing)

phases.name: Collect
phases.goal: Every paper on the list (583,596 papers in 457 journals) gets its abstract, or the text of its first pages, from the journal's own site, its school's repository, a Wayback Machine copy, or an open scholarly source.

estimate.what: Collection finishes (harvest gaps queue and CORE lane)
estimate.assumes: Rates measured on 2026-11-13: the harvest's gaps queue (about 207,500 papers) falls fast enough for about 2026-12-01, while the harvest's own estimate at 14 s a paper is about 2026-12-17 (it was 7 s a paper at noon; archive.org allows about 15 requests a minute); the CORE lane does 14-18 papers a minute for about 368,000 papers (2026-11-27 to 2026-12-02). About 10 days only if both run at their best measured pace. No long outage and no reinstall pause.

steps.name: Semantic Scholar datasets
steps.detail: Reads the papers, abstracts and full-text parts offline, then pairs what it kept with the list.
steps.needs: Keeps running until its last part and the pairing step are done (hours).

steps.name: CORE lane
steps.detail: Looks up the papers still without a text in CORE, by OAI id, DOI or title.
steps.needs: Keeps running (its keep-alive restarts it); about 2-3 weeks at today's pace.

steps.name: Journal harvest
steps.detail: Journals' own sites, school repositories and Wayback copies; one request at a time per site, about 15-25 requests a minute in all (archive.org allows about 15 a minute).
steps.needs: Keeps running until its gaps queue is empty (its keep-alive restarts it).

progress.unit: papers of the gaps queue tried

eta.basis: the harvest's own estimate (10.9 s a paper)

steps.name: Count what is still missing
steps.detail: The exact number of papers still without a text, by journal and reason; then decide on the last gap.
steps.needs: The harvest and the CORE lane finished.

phases.name: Labels
phases.goal: Subject labels to train and test the model: taxonomy 0.2.2 (78 subjects in 15 groups), coded by independent Claude coders, with adjudication where three coders read a paper.

estimate.assumes: About 7 five-hour usage windows (5.6 for the 10,000 papers, 1.1 for the doubled 2,000), one or two dedicated windows a day.

steps.name: Taxonomy 0.2.2
steps.detail: 78 subjects (leaves) in 15 groups, with a codebook.

steps.name: Pilot coding
steps.detail: 300 papers, 3 coders and an adjudicator under codebook 0.2.2; the coders agree on the top subject almost always (rank-1 Fleiss' kappa 0.99). It set the coding rules used since.

steps.name: DEV coding
steps.detail: 1,580 papers in 63 batches, 3 coders and an adjudicator each. DEV chooses the model.

steps.name: Silver S1 coding (training labels)
steps.detail: 10,000 training papers, one coder each; 2,000 of them coded a second time in a later window (SILVER-VAL).
steps.needs: About 7-8 five-hour usage windows (about 40 units a window), one coding workflow per window; the doubled 2,000 only in a window after the first pass is final.

steps.name: TEST coding
steps.detail: Paused on 2026-11-13 after its first 25 batches; it resumes after silver S1. TEST stays sealed until the final report.
steps.needs: Silver S1 finished; about 14 more usage windows.

steps.name: More silver (S2, S3)
steps.detail: More training labels, coded the same way as S1; a fourth set only if the third still helps.
steps.needs: The contest's first results.

phases.name: Model
phases.goal: Our own model: an abstract or first pages in, ranked subject tags out. Four of our architectures compete; a pre-registered rule picks the winner on DEV.

estimate.what: Contest trained on S1 and the winner chosen on DEV
estimate.assumes: 2-4 days of training on this Mac after S1, one model job at a time.

steps.name: Four architectures built and tested
steps.detail: CLARK, ULMFiT AWD-LSTM, GAN-BERT-CLARK and CLARK-G; none trained on real labels yet.

steps.name: Preview model and local test page
steps.detail: A quick model on the frozen embeddings already on disk, so tags can be tried now. Never a contest entry; its numbers are never the paper's.

steps.name: Contest training on silver S1
steps.detail: Each architecture trained on the S1 labels.
steps.needs: Silver S1 coded; one model job at a time; the harvest keeps memory priority. About 2-4 days on this Mac.

steps.name: Choose the winner on DEV
steps.detail: The registered selection rule, on the complete DEV set.
steps.needs: Contest training done.

steps.name: Tag every paper that has a text
steps.detail: The winner tags every paper that has a text.
steps.needs: The winner. Papers that get a text later are tagged when the collection ends.

phases.name: Beta release (v0.9)
phases.goal: A working product to audit: the contest winner, trained on silver S1 and chosen on DEV, tags every paper that has a text; served on the test page and a private Hugging Face Space, with its DEV numbers; the owner's audit opens.

estimate.assumes: S1 and the contest as above; then about a day to tag every paper that has a text by then and a day to serve it with its DEV numbers. It does not wait for the collection: papers that get a text later are tagged again when the collection ends.
